title: Signed and Complex Measures Hahn and Jordan

items.title: A signed measure is countably additive and takes at most one infinite value
Positive, negative, and null sets for a signed measure
A complex measure is a finite-valued countably additive set function
The real and imaginary parts of a complex measure are finite signed measures, and nu = Re nu + i Im nu
items.strategy: Take real and imaginary parts of each countable-additivity equation. Finiteness is automatic because complex values are never infinite.

items.title: The total variation |nu|(E) from countable measurable partitions
A set is null for a signed measure exactly when its total variation is zero there
items.strategy: A null partition contributes only zeros, and conversely the one-piece partition of any measurable subset forces its signed measure to vanish.

items.title: Mutual singularity for signed or complex measures
A subset of a set of finite signed measure also has finite signed measure
items.strategy: Use the at-most-one-infinity clause: adding a subset value to its complement cannot produce a finite total by cancelling opposite infinities.

items.title: If a disjoint union has finite signed measure, then the signed-measure series converges absolutely
items.strategy: Every rearrangement has the same disjoint union and hence the same finite sum. The resulting unconditional convergence is absolute by the published real-series theorem.

items.title: A set of positive finite signed measure contains a positive subset of at least the same mass
items.strategy: Strip off a maximal disjoint family of negatively measured pieces. The remainder is positive, and removing nonpositive mass can only increase the value.

items.title: Hahn decomposition for signed measures, unique up to total-variation-null sets
items.strategy: Take positive sets whose values approach the supremum, union them, and use the positive-subset lemma to show the complement is negative. Symmetric-difference pieces are both positive and negative, hence variation-null.

items.title: Jordan decomposition of a signed measure into unique mutually singular positive parts
items.strategy: Define the positive and negative parts from a Hahn decomposition. Any other singular positive decomposition induces another Hahn decomposition, forcing the same two parts.

items.title: Continuity from below, and from above when one set has finite signed measure
items.strategy: Apply the published continuity theorems to the Jordan parts and subtract.

items.title: For a signed measure, total variation is nu-plus plus nu-minus, finite partitions suffice, and nu-plus and nu-minus are extremal
items.strategy: Refine any partition by the Hahn pieces to bound the variation by the Jordan parts, attain equality on the two-piece Hahn partition, and then take suprema over measurable subsets.

items.title: Every complex measure has finite total variation
items.strategy: Estimate each partition sum by the corresponding sums for the real and imaginary parts and use their signed-measure variation formulas.

items.title: The total variation of a signed or complex measure is a positive measure
items.strategy: For disjoint ambient pieces, one inequality comes from concatenating admissible partitions and the reverse inequality comes from intersecting one admissible partition with the ambient pieces.

items.title: Complex simple functions as finite sums of measurable indicators
The simple integral against a signed or complex measure
Simple integrals are bounded by total variation
items.strategy: Evaluate a simple function on a partition where it is constant and use the triangle inequality term by term.

items.title: Total variation is the supremum of simple integrals over unit-bounded test functions
items.strategy: The upper bound is the simple integral inequality. For the lower bound, choose one unit-modulus scalar on each partition piece to align the sum with the phase of the measure there.

items.title: Every L^1 function admits dominated complex simple approximations
items.strategy: Approximate the positive and negative parts of the real and imaginary components by increasing simple functions and use monotone convergence on the error terms.

items.title: Integration against a signed or complex measure, and the class L^1(nu) = L^1(|nu|)
Integrals against signed or complex measures are bounded by total variation
items.strategy: Pass the simple-function inequality to an L^1 limit along the defining approximation.

items.title: A complex L^1 density defines a complex measure whose total variation is |h| dmu
items.strategy: Countable additivity comes from the positive-measure integral. The upper bound is partitionwise, and the lower bound uses unit-bounded simple approximants to the phase of h.

items.title: The class M(X, A) of signed measures with finite total variation and the quantity ||nu|| = |nu|(X)
Finite-total-variation signed measures form a real normed space
items.strategy: Pointwise addition and scalar multiplication preserve signed measures, the partition definition gives homogeneity and subadditivity of variation, and |nu|(X) = 0 forces nu = 0.

items.title: Finite-total-variation signed measures are complete in the total-variation norm
items.strategy: A variation-Cauchy sequence is pointwise Cauchy on each measurable set. Its pointwise limit is countably additive by uniform tail control from one approximant and the variation estimates.

items.title: A real L^1 density defines a finite signed measure with Hahn sets {f > 0} and {f <= 0}, Jordan parts f-plus dmu and f-minus dmu, and total variation |f| dmu
items.strategy: Split f into positive and negative parts, use the positive-measure indefinite integral theorem for the two parts, and read the sign sets directly from the density.

title: Signed and Complex Measures Hahn and Jordan — Examples

items.title: For nu = delta_1 - delta_{-1}, the Hahn sets are {1} and {-1}, the Jordan parts are delta_1 and delta_{-1}, and ||nu|| = 2
items.strategy: Evaluate the signed measure on subsets of {1,-1}. The two atoms already separate the positive and negative masses.

items.title: For nu(E) = int_E sin x d lambda on [0,2 pi], one Hahn decomposition is [0,pi] and (pi,2 pi], while the canonical density sets are {sin x > 0} and {sin x <= 0}
items.strategy: Use the density theorem and the sign pattern of sine; the boundary zeros can be assigned either way.

items.title: The signed counting-measure density nu({k}) = (-1)^k 2^{-|k|} on Z has total variation 3
items.strategy: Use counting measure and the real-density theorem; the positive and negative masses are explicit geometric tails on the even and odd integers.

items.title: On [0,1], mu_c - lambda is already the difference of mutually singular positive measures
items.strategy: The Cantor measure lives on the Cantor set and Lebesgue measure lives off it there, so the two positive parts are already singular.

items.title: The complex measure dnu = e^{ix} d lambda on [0,2 pi] has total variation 2 pi
items.strategy: Apply the complex-density theorem with |e^{ix}| = 1 and compute the interval's Lebesgue measure.

items.title: Finite partitions need not attain complex total variation
items.strategy: Use the complex measure nu(E)=int_E e^(ix) dlambda on [0,2pi]. Every finite partition loses strict triangle inequality on each positive-measure piece, while sufficiently fine countable interval partitions produce sums arbitrarily close to the total variation 2pi.

items.title: Moving the singleton {pi} changes a Hahn decomposition of sin x d lambda without changing its total-variation class
items.strategy: In the sine-density example, {pi} is variation-null because the density vanishes there, so it can be moved between the positive and negative sides.

items.title: For nu = delta_1 - delta_{-1}, total variation of the whole set exceeds the absolute value of nu(X)
items.strategy: The Jordan parts contribute 1 + 1 while the signed cancellation leaves nu(X) = 0.

items.title: On the finite-cofinite sigma-algebra of N, a finite-valued finitely additive set function can have infinite total variation
items.strategy: Take the alternating charge that sums over finite sets and subtracts the finite-complement sum over cofinite sets; partitions into many singletons make the variation arbitrarily large.

items.title: FALSE: a signed measure may take both +infty and -infty
items.strategy: If disjoint measurable A and B had those values, countable additivity on A union B would require the undefined sum +infty + (-infty).

items.title: FALSE: a Hahn decomposition is unique
items.strategy: The sine-density example lets the variation-null singleton {pi} move from one side to the other.

items.title: FALSE: for every signed measure and measurable E, |nu|(E) = |nu(E)|
items.strategy: For delta_1 - delta_{-1} on the whole two-point set, the right side is 0 while the left side is 2.

items.title: FALSE: signed measures agreeing on a generating pi-system are always equal
items.strategy: Counting measure and counting measure plus delta_0 agree on every nonempty open interval, which generate the Borel sigma-algebra, but differ at {0}.

items.title: FALSE: a finite-valued finitely additive set function must have finite total variation
items.strategy: The alternating charge on the finite-cofinite sigma-algebra is finite-valued and finitely additive, but partitions into many singletons make its total variation arbitrarily large.

items.title: FALSE: finite partitions always suffice to compute the total variation of a complex measure
items.strategy: The atomic complex measure with phases e^{i/(n+1)} has total variation 1 by the singleton partition, but every finite partition loses mass on a cell with at least two distinct phases.
